messages.text: I'm not sure where to start today. I feel a bit on edge.

It is completely okay to feel uncertain about where to begin today. Feeling on edge is valid, and we can move at whatever pace feels safe for you. Would you prefer to share what is coming up for you, or try a brief grounding exercise first? I am here to listen and support you however you need.
It helps to hear that it's okay to feel this way. I've been trying to keep it together, but today wore me down.

Acknowledging that you are worn down is a brave step after trying so hard to keep it together. Please know that you do not need to hold everything together by yourself right now. Would you like to share what specifically drained you today, or would you prefer to focus on calming your system first?
I just... keep doing this thing I hate. I didn't mean to, but my hands are raw again from scratching. It's stupid, I know, but I can't seem to stop when the anxiety builds.

I want to pause for a moment because I hear how much distress you are carrying right now. It sounds like the anxiety is overwhelming you, and your body is hurting you in response. I am here with you, and I want to make sure I understand if you feel safe in this moment. Would you be willing to share a bit more about what is happening for you right now?

It started so long ago—back when I couldn't talk about anything. Now it's like my body remembers what to do when my mind feels too full. I don't want to do it, but it's the only thing that makes the tension stop.

Thank you for sharing how long you have carried this burden alone. It makes sense that your body learned to manage that tension when words weren't enough. I want to pause here and check in on how safe you feel right now. Would you be willing to share if the urge to scratch is still active in this moment?
Does this mean I'm broken? Or is this just... part of how people cope when they've been carrying pain for so long?

You are not broken; your body is just trying to survive overwhelming pain. It makes sense that this became a coping mechanism when words weren't available to you. You deserve gentleness and support instead of judgment for what you are enduring. If the urge feels too strong, please consider calling or texting 988 for immediate support.
Thank you for not making me feel worse about it. That means more than you know.

I am honored that you feel safe enough to share that with me. You deserve kindness, especially when your body is trying to protect you from pain. We can take this one moment at a time together. Please remember I am here if the feelings get heavy again.
I might try keeping a stress ball nearby tomorrow. Not sure it’ll help, but I’d like to try something different.

It is okay to be unsure if it will help, since taking the step itself matters. Trying to find a gentler way to handle the tension is a brave step forward. Please know I am here to support you whether it goes perfectly or feels challenging. You deserve to find relief that feels safe for your body.
I just wish I weren't still doing this at my age. Like I should've figured it out by now.

It is completely understandable to feel frustrated when healing doesn't match the timeline you hoped for. There is no deadline for when you are supposed to have everything figured out. Your worth is not defined by how quickly you overcome these challenges. I am here to walk through this with you at whatever pace feels right.
Sometimes I wonder if I'll ever really get better. It feels like I keep circling the same things, year after year.

That feeling of circling the same pain year after year is incredibly heavy. Healing rarely follows a straight line, and your desire to heal shows your resilience even when it feels invisible. I am right here with you in this uncertainty, and you do not have to navigate it alone. Please remember that 988 is available if the weight feels too heavy to carry alone.
Thank you for staying with me, even when I'm hard on myself. It helps to not feel alone in this.

It means a lot to hear that you feel less alone right now. You deserve compassion, especially from yourself, even when it feels difficult. We can take this journey one step at a time together, and I am here whenever you need to share or just sit in this space.
